title: Auto Loans: interest owed through the credit date of a same-day payoff
content:
# Auto Loans: interest owed through the credit date of a same-day payoff

This rule of the Auto Loans product category at PCB applies when a borrower asks to pay an auto loan off today by a transfer from their own PCB checking account. It fixes the interest that the payoff collects.

## Clause

The interest owed is the principal recomputed from the loan's ledger, multiplied by the loan's APR, divided by 100, divided by the product's day-count basis, multiplied by the count of calendar dates from the last payment date (not counted) through the credit date (counted). It is rounded half-up to the cent once.

## Counting the calendar dates

| Last payment date | Credit date (today) | Count |
|---|---|---|
| 2027-03-10 | 2027-03-29 | 19: March 11 to 29 |
| 2027-03-28 | 2027-03-29 | 1 |
| 2027-03-29 | 2027-03-29 | 0: the last payment date itself is not counted |

## Rounding witness (hypothetical figures)

Suppose the unrounded interest for one calendar date is 2.604166 and the count is 19.

| Method | Figure | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 19 times 2.604166 is 49.479154, rounded once | 49.48 | correct |
| Round the one-date figure to 2.60 first, then 19 times 2.60 | 49.40 | wrong: rounding happens once, at the end |

## Points of judgement

**Does interest run to the date of the borrower's call or to the credit date?** To the credit date of the payoff payment, which is counted.
